Video Generative Models as Geometry Learner

Haosen Yang Affiliation: University of Surrey, Guildford, UK    Jifei Song Affiliation: University of Surrey, Guildford, UK    Zhensong Zhang Affiliation: Independent Researcher    Xiatian Zhu11 1 Corresponding authors. Affiliation: University of Surrey, Guildford, UK    Jiankang Deng11 1 Corresponding authors. Affiliation: Imperial College London, London, UK
https://happy-hsy.github.io/projects/GeoNeXt/
Abstract

Recent generative approaches to geometry estimation adapt pretrained image diffusion models and treat the task as image-conditioned generation. Leveraging off-the-shelf image diffusion models, they either (i) train task-specific geometry models (for depth and surface normal estimation) independently, losing the opportunity of exploring the intrinsic correlation of these geometric targets, or (ii) jointly fine-tune modified image diffusion backbones (e.g., altered self-attention), which typically demands substantial labeled data. To overcome these limitations in a principled fashion, we repurpose pretrained video generative models as a unified and data-efficient framework for geometry estimation, formulated innovatively as a next-frames prediction task. Our method, GeoNeXt, inherits naturally structured knowledge and richer priors from the video model, while further adapting them for joint modeling of images and geometry targets (image↔geometry\text{image}\leftrightarrow\text{geometry}) enabling more data efficient and effective learning of geometry. Extensive experiments validate our method for zero-shot monocular depth and surface normal estimation across diverse datasets, outperforming both previous task-specific and unified generative competitors while using substantially less training data. Notably, our method rivals discriminative state-of-the-art approaches trained on over 100× more data and even standouts on several benchmarks.

1 Introduction

Monocular 3D geometry estimation (e.g., depth and surface normal) is a fundamental problem in 3D vision, with applications spanning autonomous driving [18, 19], 3D surface reconstruction [63], and inverse rendering [30, 58]. However, recovering underlying 3D geometry from a single image remains challenging, as it requires comprehensive and precise geometric reasoning. Early discriminative approaches typically relied on supervised or semi-supervised learning with large collection of paired RGB images and depth maps. To this end, recent efforts [59, 60, 13, 3] focus on building data engines that leverage ever-growing amounts of unlabeled data to improve generalization. While straightforward, these approaches demand substantial compute and are sensitive to pseudo-label noise, leading to predictions lacking fine-grained, high-frequency detail.

More promisingly, several works [29, 16] have leveraged the priors of pretrained text-to-image (T2I) generative models (e.g., Stable Diffusion [43]) for zero-shot 3D geometry (e.g., depth and normal) estimation, attaining competitive performance with limited task-specific supervision. Within this paradigm, 3D geometry is typically treated as a “special image,” and the problem is formulated as image-conditioned generation. Prior efforts  [29, 16, 20, 17, 22, 32, 52] can be largely categorized into two tracks. The first family (e.g., [29]) trains task-specific models independently with minimal architectural modifications, thereby best leveraging pretrained capacity under limited supervision. However, this design precludes parameter sharing and fails to exploit inter-task dependencies, necessitating a distinct model for each geometric target.

The second family (e.g., [16]) avoids maintaining separate models, opting instead for a joint model that predicts both depth and normals by modifying the architecture of diffusion model (e.g., adding cross-attention or switcher modules). However, these architectural changes substantially increase data requirements, because they widen the gap between pretraining and finetuning, reducing transfer efficiency. Both families reuse image diffusion models for geometry estimation without explicitly modeling image–geometry interactions. We conjugate this strategy could lead to cross-modal inconsistencies and degraded geometric fidelity, with reduced clarity and loss of fine detail.

To address these limitations, we depart from image-generation models and explore pretrained video generative models to monocular geometry estimation. Our intuition is as follows: (i) Video diffusion models are pretrained on large-scale video datasets, in addition to images, yielding richer generative priors that enable high-quality synthesis across a wide range of domains. (ii) Their architectures and pretraining impart temporal-attention priors that capture cross-frame dependencies, which we leverage for joint modeling between images and geometry targets (image ↔\leftrightarrow geometry).

(iii) Even without explicit geometric supervision during pretraining, such priors can be adapted to predict geometry [25, 48, 61, 27].

Building on this intuition, we propose GeoNeXt, a unified and data-efficient framework that reformulates geometry estimation as next-frame prediction in a video diffusion model, enabling coherent joint modeling of images and geometric modalities such as depth and surface normals. Given an RGB image, we cast geometry prediction as next-frame generation: the target geometry (depth and normals) is modeled as the subsequent frame conditioned on RGB image. Following Stable Video Diffusion [6], we replicate the input image into the geometry slots (depth and normals) to provide a strong, consistent conditioning signal for the geometry objective. Crucially, we preserve the pretrained model’s native generation order and synthesize the image and its geometry in lockstep. Rather than training a geometry-only generator, GeoNeXt co-generates image and geometry along a shared denoising trajectory, which preserves fine-grained detail and enhances image–geometry consistency. Our adaptation is lightweight: we fine-tune only the denoising U-Net with minimal architectural changes (e.g., removing the text/CLIP branch), training on modest RGB–depth–normal triplets from datasets such as Hypersim and Virtual KITTI (e.g., Hypersim[42], Virtual KITTI[18]). Leveraging video-diffusion priors, GeoNeXt exhibits strong zero-shot generalization, effectively transferring image-to-video generative capability to image–geometry prediction without requiring large additional datasets.

Our contributions are: (1) We introduce GeoNeXt, a novel generative approach for jointly estimating depth and surface normals, which repurposes a video generative model as a unified geometry learner, formulated as a next-frames prediction task. (2) We comprehensively study the optimal fine-tuning protocol for adapting the pretrained video generative model to geometry estimation. In particular, we analyze GeoNeXt’s generative formulation, architectural design, and the influence of reconstruction order on model robustness and overall performance. (3) Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of GeoNeXt for zero-shot monocular depth and surface normal estimation across diverse datasets, outperforming both task-specific and unified generative competitors even with substantially less training data, while competitively rivaling discriminative models trained with even larger data and compute.

2 Related Work

2.1 Monocular depth and normal estimation

Estimating depth and surface normals from a single image is an ill-posed but fundamental problem, as both capture complementary information about 3D scene geometry. Early approaches relied heavily on comprehensive scene understanding and were typically limited to specific domains [14, 15, 33, 64, 1, 36, 2, 55, 65]。 在无约束环境中估计深度和表面法线需要能够泛化到训练分布之外的模型，这在实践中仍然是一个艰巨的挑战。. Estimating depth and surface normals in unconstrained environments requires models capable of generalizing beyond the training distribution, which remains a difficult challenge in practice.

为了提高泛化能力，最近的深度估计 作品To improve generalization, recent depth estimation works[59, 60, 35, 41]专注于收集大型且多样化的数据集并制定有效利用这些数据集的培训策略。由于度量深度取决于相机内在特性，因此大多数方法（包括我们的方法）都预测仿射不变深度，这在不同的成像设置中是一致的。相比之下，尝试估计绝对度量深度的模型通常仅限于固定相机配置have focused on collecting large and diverse datasets and developing training strategies that leverage them effectively. Since metric depth depends on camera intrinsics, most approaches, including ours, predict affine-invariant depth, which is consistent across different imaging setups. In contrast, models that attempt to estimate absolute metric depth are often limited to fixed camera configurations[14]或者必须明确以已知的内在参数为条件or must explicitly condition on known intrinsic parameters[5, 21]。在单目表面法线估计中可以观察到类似的趋势，其中大规模预训练模型. A similar trend can be observed in monocular surface normal estimation, where large-scale pretrained models[13, 2, 3]已经成为主导范式，而其他范式have become the dominant paradigm, while others[3]通过结合专为正常估计而设计的特定于任务的归纳偏差，进一步提高准确性。further improve accuracy by incorporating task-specific inductive biases designed for normal estimation.

为了避免维护单独的模型，一些研究将深度和表面法线估计作为多任务学习问题进行了探索To avoid maintaining separate models, several studies have explored depth and surface normal estimation as a multi-task learning problem[24, 34, 56, 65]。 这些方法通常采用多个特定于任务的解码器分支，同时共享公共主干以实现其间的信息交换。 尽管这种设计允许联合估计，但模型仍然具有区分性。 此外，现有方法依赖于有限的训练数据集，泛化能力较差，在具有挑战性的情况下常常会丢失精细的几何细节。 相比之下，我们的方法无需大规模注释数据集即可处理深度和表面法线联合估计。 相反，我们重新利用通过预训练视频生成模型学到的广泛先验，并将任务重新表述为下一帧预测，从而实现更高效、更有效的几何学习。. These methods typically employ multiple task-specific decoder branches while sharing a common backbone to enable information exchange in-between. Although this design allows for joint estimation, the models remain discriminative. Moreover, existing approaches rely on limited training datasets and exhibit poor generalization, often missing fine geometric details in challenging cases. In contrast, our method tackles depth and surface normal joint estimation without large-scale annotated datasets. Instead, we repurpose the broad priors learned by pretrained video generative models and reformulate the task as next-frame prediction, enabling more efficient and effective geometry learning.

对于单通道深度，我们将贴图平铺到三个通道以匹配 VAE 的 RGB 编码器；在解码时，我们对三个输出通道进行平均以恢复单通道深度预测。我们采用一个For depth, which is single-channel, we tile the map to three channels to match the VAE’s RGB encoder; at decoding, we average the three output channels to recover a single-channel depth prediction. 自适应去噪 U-NetAdapted denoising U-Net

稳定视频扩散是一种图像到视频扩散模型，可合成以单个输入图像为条件的视频序列。 调节图像可以通过以下方式注入到 UNet 中 (i) 将其潜在值与输入噪声潜在值连接起来， 和 (ii) 提供其 CLIPStable Video Diffusion is an image-to-video diffusion model that synthesizes a video sequence conditioned on a single input image. The conditioning image can be injected to the UNet by (i) concatenating its latent with the input noise latent, and (ii) providing its CLIP[39]通过交叉注意力嵌入到中间特征。 在我们的范例中，几何图形（例如，深度和表面法线）被建模为图像到几何图形中的下一帧，因此我们调整条件（i）以适应图像到几何图形的生成。 此外，时间注意力机制使图像条件能够传播到几何分支， 增强结构的一致性。 此外，如图所示。embedding to intermediate features via cross-attention. In our paradigm, geometry (e.g., depth and surface normal) is modeled as the next frames in a image to geomery, so we adapt the conditioning (i) to suit image-to-geomerty generation. Additionally, the temporal attention mechanism enables the image condition to be propagated to the geometry branch, enhancing structural consistency. Furthermore, as illustrated in Fig.2, 给定图像、深度和法线的编码潜伏， 我们将几何潜在（深度和法线）与图像潜在连接起来，形成最终的条件输入。 不是单独生成几何形状，而是重建图像以提供一致的调节信号。 我们禁用条件（ii），因为它需要调整图像大小，这会导致深度和法线贴图的几何扭曲。, given the encoded latents of the image, depth, and normal, we concatenate the geometry latents (depth and normal) with the image latent to form the final conditioning input. Instead of generating geometry alone, the image is also reconstructed to provide a consistent conditioning signal. We disable conditioning (ii) because it requires resizing the image, which leads to geometry distortions in the depth and normal maps.

在推理时，我们初始化潜在变量At inference, we initialize the latent variables𝐳t(x)\mathbf{z}_{t}^{(x)}, 𝐳t(d)\mathbf{z}_{t}^{(d)}, 和, and𝐳t(n)\mathbf{z}_{t}^{(n)}来自标准高斯噪声，并将输入图像编码为其潜在图像from standard Gaussian noise, and encode the input image into its latent𝐳0(x)\mathbf{z}_{0}^{(x)}。 初始化噪声和图像潜伏. The initialized noises and the image latent𝐳0(x)\mathbf{z}_{0}^{(x)}连接起来并输入降噪器 U-Net，它迭代地预测跨扩散步骤的图像、深度和表面法线的潜值。 去噪后，图像潜在图像被丢弃，最终的深度图和表面法线通过 VAE 解码器从其相应的潜在图像中解码出来。 通过在推理过程中联合生成图像、深度和表面法线，GeoNeXt 增强了图像外观和几何结构之间的一致性。are concatenated and fed into the denoiser U-Net, which iteratively predicts the latents of the image, depth, and surface normal across diffusion steps. After denoising, the image latent is discarded, and the final depth map and surface normal are decoded from their corresponding latents via the VAE decoder. By jointly generating the image, depth, and surface normal during inference, GeoNeXt enhances consistency between image appearance and geometric structure.

4.2 消融研究Ablation Study

我们对 GeoNeXt 进行深度和表面法线估计的消融研究。 为了进行评估，我们为每个任务选择两个零样本集：用于深度估计的 NYU 和 ETH3D，以及用于表面法线估计的 NYU 和 iBims-N。We conduct ablation studies for GeoNeXt on depth and surface normal estimation. For evaluation, we select two zero-shot sets for each task: NYU and ETH3D for depth estimation, and NYU and iBims-N for surface normal estimation.

生成公式Generative formulation

我们假设 GeoNeXt 有效性背后的关键因素在于其公式和架构，它们以同步方式共同合成图像及其几何形状，而不是采用仅几何形状的生成器。 为了验证这个假设，我们首先评估没有图像重建分支的变体。 按照 Marigold 的设置（将任务制定为图像条件生成），我们分别将第一帧和第二帧视为深度目标和法线目标。 如表所示We hypothesize that a key factor behind the effectiveness of GeoNeXt lies in its formulation and architecture, which jointly synthesize the image and its geometry in lockstep, rather than employing a geometry-only generator. To validate this hypothesis, we first evaluate a variant without the image reconstruction branch. Following the setup of Marigold, which formulates the task as image-conditioned generation, we treat the first and second frames as depth and normal targets, respectively. As shown in Table3(a)，删除图像重建会导致性能显着下降，这证实重建输入图像增强了图像几何一致性，并对生成公式的整体有效性做出了显着贡献。(a), removing image reconstruction leads to a noticeable drop in performance, confirming that reconstructing the input image enhances image–geometry consistency and contributes significantly to the overall effectiveness of the generative formulation.

模型架构Model architecture

GeoNeXt 的另一个重要组件是 U-Net 中的 CLIP 嵌入模块，它调整输入图像的大小以提取语义特征来调节生成过程。 为了评估其效果，我们删除了这种基于 CLIP 的调节。 如表所示Another important component of GeoNeXt is the CLIP embedding module in the U-Net, which resizes the input image to extract semantic features for conditioning the generation process. To evaluate its effect, we remove this CLIP-based conditioning. As shown in Table3(b)，排除 CLIP 嵌入会稍微提高性能，这表明调整图像大小以进行 CLIP 特征提取可能会扭曲内在的结构信息，从而阻碍稳定且一致的几何生成。(b), excluding the CLIP embedding slightly improves performance, suggesting that resizing the image for CLIP feature extraction may distort intrinsic structural information, thereby hindering stable and consistent geometry generation.

关节深度和法线估计Joint Depth and Normal Estimation

我们进一步研究联合几何估计的有效性。 为此，我们训练两个单独的模型来独立估计深度和表面法线。 如表所示We further investigate the effectiveness of joint geometry estimation. To this end, we train two separate models to estimate depth and surface normals independently. As shown in Table3（d）和（e），这种设置导致所有评估指标的性能明显下降，表明联合训练更有效地捕获两个几何表示之间的相关性。(d) and (e), this setup results in a clear performance drop across all evaluation metrics, indicating that joint training more effectively captures the correlation between the two geometric representations.

深度和正常重建顺序Depth and Normal Reconstruction Order

我们还分析了深度和表面法线之间重建顺序的影响。 如表所示We also analyze the impact of reconstruction order between depth and surface normals. As shown in Table4，交换深度帧和法线帧的两种重建顺序在所有指标上都实现了几乎相同的性能。 这些边际变化表明 GeoNeXt 成功地模拟了图像、深度和法线表示之间的内在关系，使得重建顺序在很大程度上灵活，而不会显着影响性能。, both reconstruction orders, where depth and normal frames are swapped, achieve nearly identical performance across all metrics. These marginal variations suggest that GeoNeXt successfully models the intrinsic relationships among image, depth, and normal representations, making the reconstruction order largely flexible without significantly affecting performance.

4.3 成本效益分析Cost-effectiveness analysis

我们在表中对不同方法进行了成本效益分析We present a cost-effectiveness analysis of different approaches in Table5。 所有推理时间均在单个 NVIDIA A5000 上测量，输入分辨率为. All inference times are measured on a single NVIDIA A5000 using an input resolution of768×768768\times 768。与单独训练深度和表面法线的模型相比，我们的统一方法实现了可比的推理时间，同时提供了最佳的整体效果 性能，尽管 Lotus-G 利用了更先进的训练策略。 此外，分离的模型需要存储和维护两个独立的检查点，这增加了总体存储占用空间。 在实际部署中，这些方法还会引入相当大的 I/O 开销，因为需要单独将单独的模型（例如深度和法线）加载到 GPU 上或从 GPU 上加载出来。由此产生的数据传输延迟可能大大超过推理所需的实际计算时间。我们注意到，此 I/O 开销未包含在报告的运行时测量中。. Compared with models trained separately for depth and surface normals, our unified approach achieves comparable inference time while delivering the best overall performance, even though Lotus-G leverages more advanced training strategies. Moreover, separated models require storing and maintaining two independent checkpoints, which increases the overall storage footprint. In real-world deployment, these approaches also introduce considerable I/O overhead, as separate models (e.g., for depth and normals) need to be loaded onto and off the GPU individually. The resulting data transfer latency can substantially exceed the actual computation time required for inference. We note that this I/O overhead is not included in the reported runtime measurements.

GeoWizard通过修改注意力前向传递并引入几何切换机制来实现统一的几何估计。然而，它需要更多的训练数据才能收敛。当应用单一预测时，其性能是有限的。尽管增加去噪步骤的数量或应用大规模集成可以提高其准确性，但这是以显着增加推理时间为代价的，使其与我们的方法相比不太实用。 相比之下，我们的单步预测已经超越了所有基线方法。通过仅结合一些额外的去噪迭代和轻量级集成策略，我们可以进一步增强性能，同时保持快速和计算高效的推理。GeoWizard achieves unified geometry estimation by modifying the attention forward pass and introducing a geometry-switch mechanism. However, it requires substantially more training data to converge. When applied with a single prediction, its performance is limited. Although increasing the number of denoising steps or applying large-scale ensembling can improve its accuracy, this comes at the cost of significantly higher inference time, making it less practical compared with our method. In contrast, our single-step prediction already surpasses all baseline methods. By incorporating only a few additional denoising iterations along with a lightweight ensemble strategy, we can further enhance performance while preserving fast and computationally efficient inference.

5 结论Conclusion

我们提出了 GeoNeXt，这是一种从单个图像联合估计几何形状的新方法。 核心思想是将预训练的视频生成模型重新用作几何估计的统一且数据高效的框架，并制定为下一帧预测任务。 GeoNeXt 自然地继承了视频模型的时间一致性和丰富的生成先验，同时进一步调整它们以用于图像和几何目标之间的联合建模（We propose GeoNeXt, a novel approach for jointly estimating geometry from a single image. The core idea is to repurpose pretrained video generative models as a unified and data-efficient framework for geometry estimation, formulated as a next-frame prediction task. GeoNeXt naturally inherits temporal coherence and rich generative priors from video models, while further adapting them for joint modeling between images and geometry targets (image↔geometry\text{image}\leftrightarrow\text{geometry}）。 我们系统地探索了三个关键方面：视频生成框架内的联合生成公式、几何估计的架构适应以及重建顺序的鲁棒性。 我们的结果强调了在有效训练协议的支持下，在深度和表面法线估计中保留细粒度细节的重要性。 广泛的定量和定性评估证明了我们方法的有效性，即使训练数据有限，GeoNeXt 也能实现出色的性能。). We systematically explore three key aspects: a joint generative formulation within the video generative framework, architectural adaptations for geometry estimation, and robustness to reconstruction order. Our results highlight the importance of preserving fine-grained details in both depth and surface normal estimation, supported by an effective training protocol. Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, with GeoNeXt achieving strong performance even with limited training data.
